definitions.explanation: The act of reproducing a work of art, text, or image by hand, typically for study or practice. Implies careful, faithful reproduction rather than creative reinterpretation.

examples.japanese: ⟦{名画|めいが}→名画：17385_meiga⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{模写|もしゃ}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
⟦{美術|びじゅつ}→美術：04447_bijutsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{授業|じゅぎょう}→授業：00781_jugyou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{模写|もしゃ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{練習|れんしゅう}→練習：05323_renshuu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I practiced copying in art class.

examples.japanese: ゴッホ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{若|わか}い{頃|ころ}、⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{浮世絵|うきよえ}→浮世絵：13286_ukiyoe⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{模写|もしゃ}⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{技法|ぎほう}→技法：12800_gihou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{学|まな}んだ→学ぶ：01987_manabu⟧。
examples.english: In his youth, Van Gogh copied Japanese ukiyo-e prints to learn technique.

notes:
Refers to the practice of carefully reproducing existing artwork or text by hand. In art education, {模写|もしゃ} is considered a legitimate and important method of learning technique. The word does not carry a negative connotation of plagiarism — it implies study and practice.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {模写|もしゃ}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ — to copy, to reproduce
- ⟦{名画|めいが}→名画：17385_meiga⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{模写|もしゃ} — reproduction of a masterpiece
- {模写|もしゃ}⟦{作品|さくひん}→作品：02776_sakuhin⟧ — a copied/reproduced work
- ⟦{忠実|ちゅうじつ}→忠実：12570_chuujitsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{模写|もしゃ}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ — to faithfully reproduce

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{複写|ふくしゃ}→複写：19000_fukusha⟧ — copying, duplication; mechanical reproduction (e.g., photocopying), not hand-copying
- ⟦{写生|しゃせい}→写生：04196_shasei⟧ — sketching from life; drawing from a real scene or object, not from another artwork
- ⟦{模倣|もほう}→模倣：15752_mohou⟧ — imitation; broader concept of imitating style or method, not just visual copying
- {臨書|りんしょ} — copying calligraphy; specifically for practicing calligraphy by copying a model
